caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 333 of 1997.
lawyer:
Ahmed Nowshed Jamil for Hasan Foez Siddique Advocate------ For the Appellants. 
Md Kamrul Islam Siddique with Md Bazlul Kabir Advocates------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Namita Rani Biswas and others ------ Appellants
vs
Rabindra Nath Majhi and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
7. According to the admitted case, the respondent did not claim the entire property of the testator. He claimed that Harinath Majumder gifted to his father 0.20 acres of land of plot No. 223 of SA khatian No. 225 and subsequently, on the request of his father and uncle, the testator granted them licence to possess 1.64 acres of land. Surendra Nath Biswas obtained Letter of Administration in respect of 14.86 acres of land in 8 plots. There is no dispute that after the grant he had mutated his name in the record of right, released the property from the list of Enemy Property and sold some lands to the appellants and others. Therefore, the grant has been acted upon. The respondent is not claiming the entire lands covered by the will of Harinath Majumder . Admittedly he is not an heir or the successor of Harinath Majumder. He claims that Harinath orally gifted 0.20 acres of land to his father and subsequently, he granted licence of 1.64 acres of lands to his uncle and father. In view of this admitted position, the question is, whether he can maintain an application for revocation of the grant. 

 8. The learned District Judge observed that since some lands were recorded in the SA Khatian in the name of Kalicharan, and as he possessed some lands in any capacity, he has locus standi to make an application for revocation. "But it appears that the said correction and mutation of record of right was made in the year 1985 without having any legal basis", the learned District Judge observed. The learned District Judge however observed that the khatian could be used for collateral purpose of possession. These findings are not only inconsistent but. also based upon misconception of law. The learned District Judge failed to notice that an SA Khatian has no presumptive value at all. Over and above, the respondent stated in the application that Harinath granted licence to his father and uncle in respect of 1.64 acres of land but in his deposition as PW 1 he stated that Harinath took loan of Taka 5,000 from his father and in exchange of that amount of money, he gave borga of the lands covered by SA Khatian 145 to his father and uncle. Therefore, we find inconsistent claim of the respondent in the bequeathed property. He failed to prove the basis of possession in a fractional portion of the bequeathed property. His claim of possession is dubious. In view of such inconsistent claim, the learned District Judge erred in law in believing the possession of the respondent in a portion of the lands. 

 9. A person who has an interest in the estate of the deceased is entitled to enter caveat and oppose the grant of probate or Letter of Administration, is entitled to apply for revocation. In every case in which probate or Letter of Administration of a Hindu will is asked for, a special citation ought to be served upon those persons whose interests are directly affected by the will. Although section 283 of the Succession Act does not render it obligatory on the District Delegate to issue any special citation, yet it is not only desirable but necessary in the ends of justice that this power should be exercised when it appears that some of the heirs whose interests are affected by the will. Learned Advocate for the respondent submits that even a person who has an interest however, slight, and even the bare possibility of the interest, is entitled to oppose a testamentary paper. In support of the contention he has cited some decisions. We do not dispute the contention of the learned Advocate. As observed above, the respondent failed to show even a slightest interest in the property. He claimed interest in the portion of the bequeathed property on two counts. His first claim is that Hari Nath Majumder orally gifted 0.20 acres of land to his father. The learned District Judge himself disbelieved this claim observing, "According to Hindu law, no immovable property can be transferred by way of oral gift." The other claim is that Harinath Majumder granted licence of 1.64 acres of land later on to his father and uncle on consideration of their difficulty, as the gifted plot of land was inadequate for their habitation. As observed above, the respondent has given a go-bye of his claim made in his petition and stated on oath that Harinath Majumder took Taka 5000 as loan from his father and in exchange of that amount of money, he gave borga of lands covered by SA Khatian No. 145 to his father and uncle. The respondent has totally failed to prove his possessory right on the basis of gift or licence in a portion of the bequeathed property, if there be any. The learned District Judge totally ignored the inconsistent claim of the respondent and erroneously held that he has possessory right in a portion of the bequeathed property. As the respondent had no interest in the property of the testator he was not entitled to a special citation be served at the time of issuing the grant. We hold that the grant does not displace any right to which the respondent would otherwise be entitled.
